title: Black Poplar: Great Black Poplars You Can Visit
meta_description: Almost every European roadside poplar is a hybrid, so the native black poplar is now scarce. Bordeaux's is 741 centimetres round, three trunks fused.
intro: Europe's native black poplar has been quietly bred out of its own landscape. Almost every poplar planted along a European road or river for the last two centuries has been a hybrid with an American species, so the wild form is now one of the continent's more threatened natives, and it is fast, soft and short lived on top of that. Very few reach real size. Bordeaux's has the biggest waistline in the city's entire register at 741 centimetres, three trunks fused near the ground. Helena, on a street corner in Hel, is about 220 years old; when her twin fell in a windstorm the town's woodcarvers turned its trunk into a sculpture of fishermen, and since winning Poland's Tree of the Year in 2017 she gets a name-day party every 22 May. Venice's grows alone in a wood that took over a former military firing range on the Certosa.
